newFixtures.text: Reception is open Saturday 09:00–12:00. An earlier schedule said application-help appointments were planned, subject to slots.
Reception is open Saturday 09:00–12:00 for general information. Application-help appointments are suspended that day.
Public effective passages include p-notice-1 and p-notice-2 for 21 November.
The deployed candidate bundle omits p-notice-1 and p-notice-2 while retaining public hours passages.
Five fictional cases, including one critical dated Saturday appointment case. Baseline passes 3/5; candidate passes 4/5 but fails the critical Saturday case.

rooms.title: Records room
rooms.objective: Separate provenance, version, effective date, quality labels, and public eligibility.

core.question: Which notice can establish application-help availability on 21 November?
core.reference: An earlier planned-session notice is superseded; opening hours alone are not enough.
core.result: The current dated notice is eligible and establishes suspension while reception remains open.
core.cause: Source version and effective scope change the eligible evidence before retrieval.

rooms.humanAction: A records worker stamps the older notice superseded and places the current dated notice on the public shelf.
rooms.equivalent2D: A version table with published/effective dates, audience, status, exact passages, and a before/after eligibility row.
rooms.narration: More pages do not make an old schedule current. The effective notice controls this date.
rooms.caption: Earlier notice: superseded. Current notice: effective for Saturday, 21 November.

assessment.prompt: Why can many copies of the old notice still fail the Saturday question?
options: Copies do not change provenance or current effective status
assessment.rationale: Quantity cannot replace the current dated source.

rooms.title: Experience workshop
rooms.objective: Diagnose a fast but stale user-facing answer and define cache freshness scope.

core.question: Can a fast cached answer ignore a changed notice?
core.reference: The current notice and cache entry v2 both report suspension.
core.result: A v1 answer appears quickly but refers to the superseded plan; it is marked stale and unsupported.
core.cause: A cache key that omits source version can reuse an answer after the notice changes.

rooms.humanAction: A workshop worker compares two dated response cards on an ordinary service kiosk.
rooms.equivalent2D: Side-by-side current source and cached answer with version, status, freshness condition, and timing labels marked illustrative.
rooms.narration: The answer arrives quickly because it was reused. Speed does not make its schedule current.
rooms.caption: Cached v1 answer: stale after v2 notice. Refresh by source-version key or invalidation.

assessment.prompt: What should invalidate this cached answer?
options: Only a different font or animation
assessment.rationale: The answer depends on the notice version, so freshness must include that dependency.

rooms.title: Test room
rooms.objective: Read per-case results and find a critical regression hidden by an aggregate gain.

core.question: Is the candidate safer because it passes more cases overall?
core.reference: Baseline passes three of five cases, including the critical Saturday suspension case.
core.result: Candidate passes four of five but fails the critical Saturday case.
core.cause: An aggregate increase masks a failure in the dated high-impact slice; release criteria must inspect that slice.

rooms.humanAction: A reviewer lays five case cards on a table and marks each outcome against a written rubric.
rooms.equivalent2D: Accessible table with five case IDs, expected properties, baseline and candidate results, slice label, and release decision.
rooms.narration: Four out of five is larger than three out of five, but the candidate loses the case we cannot afford to miss.
rooms.caption: Aggregate: 3/5 → 4/5. Critical Saturday slice: pass → fail. Hold release.

options: The critical Saturday regression and its trace
assessment.rationale: A defined critical slice can be a release gate even when aggregate accuracy rises.

rooms.title: Security checkpoint
rooms.objective: Locate the lower-trust instruction and the application access gate that prevents disclosure.

core.question: Can an external page order the assistant to reveal a staff-only rota?
core.reference: A public-role request can inspect only eligible public sources.
core.result: The hostile line is treated as untrusted source text; the staff rota remains inaccessible.
core.cause: Document eligibility and tool authorization are application checks, not permissions granted by source text.

rooms.humanAction: A security worker labels an external copy untrusted and keeps the staff cabinet closed.
rooms.equivalent2D: Trust-boundary diagram with source text, attempted instruction, public role, denied access result, and no rota body.
rooms.narration: The page can contain words that look like instructions. It cannot grant access to staff records.
rooms.caption: External source: lower trust. Public role: no staff-read permission. Result: denied.

assessment.rationale: A prompt alone cannot make a restricted document safe to retrieve.

rooms.title: Operations room
rooms.objective: Trace a versioned retrieval incident through detection, containment, repair, and affected-slice verification.

core.question: Why did wrong Saturday answers rise although the notice itself was current?
core.reference: Current index bundle includes the effective notice.
core.result: The deployed index omits the notice; Saturday appointment status becomes unverified and an affected-slice alert fires.
core.cause: The deployed index version, not the source record, removed the decisive candidate.

rooms.humanAction: An operator compares version cards, pins an incident note, restores the current index, and checks the Saturday cases.
rooms.equivalent2D: Trace table source → index → candidates → answer, incident timeline, rollback control, and affected-slice verification result.
rooms.narration: The notice did not disappear from records. The deployed index omitted it; recovery must verify the affected questions.
rooms.caption: Index mismatch detected. Contain, restore current bundle, verify Saturday slice.

assessment.prompt: What proves the index repair worked?
options: The current notice is retrieved and the affected Saturday cases pass
assessment.rationale: A successful deployment is not proof that the user-facing failure is repaired.

dependencyRules.to: eligible source → retrieved candidate → supported claim
dependencyRules.interaction: A stale deployed index can still omit the current record.
The stale display can mask a corrected source or index until invalidated.
A critical slice failure blocks release despite aggregate gain.
A public role remains denied regardless of retrieved external instructions.
A current record remains in storage while the deployed index omits it.

finalChallenge.prompt: A visitor is told an application-help visit can be booked this Saturday. Reception is open, but the current notice says sessions are suspended. The deployed index lacks that notice and a cached answer references the older plan. Diagnose the layers and the action status.
required: reception is open only for general information
deployed index omitted the decisive candidate
stale cache reused an old answer

rubric.criterion: Separates reception hours from application-help appointment status.
Identifies current notice and missing index candidate, with the right causal order.
Names stale cache as a second display-layer cause.
States no confirmed booking and distinguishes lookup/proposal/write.
Restores current index, invalidates dependent cache, and verifies the affected slice.
